title: Skrabalai
summary: Skrabalai are tuned wooden bell-boxes, each a hollow wooden case with a wooden clapper, hung on a timber rack. A player shakes or strikes them in turn, and the set rings with a bright, hollow knock.
howToPlay: Eight wooden bells are lit: four large ones on the lower bar, four small on the upper bar.
Strike the bell a closing ring marks. It rocks and its clapper knocks.
The larger the box, the lower the knock.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Each box is carved and shaped to a pitch, then hung in a row. Wooden bells carry sound across a farm, and a whole set can play a tune.
credits: Tradition: the skrabalai of Lithuania; patterns written for this game
